title: The Inca ran a vast empire on records tied in knots
body: The Inca Empire had no writing in the usual sense, yet it tracked taxes, census counts and calendars across the Andes using quipus: bundles of cotton or camelid-fiber cords. Knots tied in a decimal positional system stored numbers, while color and cord order added categories. Trained specialists called quipucamayocs read them, and courts accepted them as records. Whether some quipus also encoded words is still debated.
